title: Strata landed or individual title: which kind of landed home to buy?
videoTitle: STRATA VS INDIVIDUAL TITLE LANDED HOMES | KEYNOTE IN ECO HORIZON
excerpt: At a talk in Batu Kawan, Sean explains the difference between gated landed strata homes and traditional individual-title houses, from security and maintenance to who will buy at RM1.8 million.

qa.context: Landed homes in Malaysia come in two main forms: traditional individual-title houses on public roads, and newer landed strata developments with a guardhouse, shared landscaping and a management body. Sean answered this question at a talk in a landed strata township in Batu Kawan, Penang, drawing on a strata home he bought in Johor Bahru eight years earlier.
qa.question: What is the difference between landed strata and individual-title homes, and which holds its value better?
qa.quote: the least I expect from a house is actually security
qa.answer: Landed strata costs more up front and comes with rules and maintenance fees, but gives security, planned infrastructure and a say over the neighbourhood. Sean expects most future landed homes to be strata, and individual-title prices to hit a ceiling because buyers at that level expect security.

reasons.title: You pay for planning
reasons.body: The developer has to plan landscaping, facilities, roads, drains and metering up front, so strata homes cost more. Individual-title houses are quicker and simpler to build, which is why developers once preferred them.

reasons.title: Rules limit renovation
reasons.body: When Sean bought his strata home for about RM1.8 million, he found he couldn't change the facade or colours freely. Managements have since become more flexible about kitchen extensions and other changes.

reasons.title: Individual titles hide their upkeep
reasons.body: Owners of traditional houses often defer repairs to water tanks, gates and paint until a buyer complains. In strata, a management team maintains the estate, and owners can vote on uses such as a neighbour's house becoming a temple.

reasons.title: Who buys at RM1.8 million?
reasons.body: A household needs about RM24,000 a month to afford an RM1.8 million house. Buyers at that level expect layered security, which an open street can't give; some wealthy owners are downsizing into secure apartments instead.

actions: Ask what renovations and facade changes the management allows.
Budget for maintenance fees, and compare them with the hidden upkeep of an older house.
Check what infrastructure surrounds the plot, such as sewage plants or substations.
Compare commute times; landed homes are often far from city jobs.
For an own-stay home, check that local rents cover about 85% of the instalment.
qa.caveat: In Penang, land scarcity on the island means Sean would put a larger budget into commercial or industrial property rather than more high-rise. His views on individual-title prices are, by his own account, unpopular.

sourceNote: Summarised from the first part of Sean's English captions for this 1 hour 51 minute question-and-answer session, held at a developer's landed strata project in Batu Kawan; later questions on other topics are not covered. Sean says he owns units in other projects by the same developer. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased.
